retainedBefore.name: ExteNet Systems
retainedBefore.description: ExteNet develops and operates outdoor and in-building wireless infrastructure, fiber networks, and related connectivity systems for mobile carriers, venue owners, and enterprise customers. The company follows an asset-heavy model built around long-lived communications infrastructure and recurring carrier or venue revenues rather than retail service revenues. Public materials describe ExteNet as the largest privately held U.S. provider focused on DAS, small cells, fiber, and other advanced connectivity solutions. Its footprint is national, and the company relocated its headquarters to Frisco, Texas while continuing to serve carrier and enterprise customers across major U.S. markets. John Hancock led the acquisition of an approximately 30% stake in 2020, and ExteNet announced the closing of the Manulife-led investment in 2021 alongside existing owners Digital Colony and Stonepeak. Manulife's infrastructure team identifies the investment with Fund II.

retiredDuplicate.name: Extenet
retiredDuplicate.subsector: Distributed wireless and fiber connectivity infrastructure
retiredDuplicate.description: Extenet designs, builds, owns, and operates distributed wireless and fiber connectivity infrastructure across North America. Its customers include wireless carriers, venue owners, enterprises, and public-sector users that require indoor and outdoor mobility infrastructure rather than retail broadband services. The operating model is asset-heavy and contract based, supported by small cells, distributed antenna systems, and associated fiber networks with long useful lives. Company materials describe the business as one of the largest privately held communications infrastructure providers in North America and list a headquarters in Frisco, Texas. Stonepeak and DigitalBridge led a recapitalization of ExteNet in 2015, Manulife announced a strategic investment in 2021, and the company rebranded as Extenet in 2022.
